title: Switzerland – Architectural and related services – Ausbildungszentrum Riedikon, Neubau Logistik- und Verwaltungszentrum
description: Auf dem Grundstück Kat.-Nr. L1340, Bühlenweg 20 in Riedikon, betreibt die Leistungsgruppe Bevölkerungsschutz der Stadt Uster ein Ausbildungszentrum. Die Grundstücksfläche umfasst total 28'573 m2, wovon für das Ausbildungszentrum 10'400 m2, für die Vermietung an den Hundeclub 4600 m2 und für die landwirtschaftliche Verpachtung 9300 m2 genutzt werden. 4273 m2 sind Restfläche mit Wald und Moor. Das Ausbildungszentrum besteht aus diversen Übungsgebäuden und -flächen, sowie den zugehörigen Garderoben-, Schulungs-, Verwaltungs- und Lagerräumen. Die beiden Brandhäuser wurden in den vergangenen Jahren neu erstellt und sind auf dem neuesten Stand. Die Nebengebäude sind teilweise in einem schlechten Zustand und dringend sanierungsbedürftig. Mit dem Unterpachtvertrag für das Areal Zeughaus West an eine gemeinnützige Wohnbaugenossenschaft muss der Zivilschutz in absehbarer Zeit dieses Areal verlassen und benötigt neue Einstellflächen für die Fahrzeuge und einen Ort für den Zusammenzug. Aus diesen beiden Gründen wurde entschieden, das Ausbildungszentrum um ein neues Logistik- und Verwaltungszentrum zu erweitern. So kann der gesamte Zivilschutz an einem zentralen Ort untergebracht und Schulungen abgehalten werden.

title: Biometric Capture Device GWAC
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with RFO FAR Part 12 in conjunction with the procedures, as appropriate, at RFO FAR Part 15, and as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested and a written solicitation is hereby issued as part of this notice. The anticipated Biometric Capture Devices solicitation shall be issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP) where RFO FAR provision 52.212-1 and clause 52.212-4 apply. Additional provisions, clauses, terms and conditions, to include evaluation factors and the basis for award, are in the Solicitation. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Office of Procurement Operations (OPO) issues this Request for Proposals (RFP) to establish government-wide, multiple-award indefinite-delivery indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contracts for biometric capture devices and peripheral equipment. The IDIQ contracts will permit Firm Fixed-Price orders. The period of performance will consist of a one-year base period and four one-year option periods. The dates of the periods of performance will be established at contract award. See Section F. The Biometric Capture Devices solicitation will be available for full and open competition with the anticipation that multiple awards will be made within each of the five (5) device tracks, Fingerprint, Facial, Iris, Palmprint, and Multi-Modal. For each track, the Government anticipates establishing a minimum of three (3) and maximum of unlimited IDIQ contracts with Offerors submitting an overall proposal that is determined to be best value to the Government utilizing a Highest Technically Rated with a Fair and Reasonable Price award basis. These numbers are estimates, and DHS may increase or decrease the number of awards in its sole discretion. In determining the number of awards, DHS�s intent is to ensure beneficial competition occurs at the delivery order level while maximizing the effectiveness and efficiency of the BCD program. Proposal submission and evaluation details are provided within Sections L and M of this solicitation. Multiple Proposals Interested offerors may submit proposals for one or more of the five BCD award tracks. Each award track requires a separate proposal. Accordingly, an offeror that wishes to compete under multiple tracks shall submit a separate proposal for each track. Within a single track, an offeror may propose more than one device that satisfies the requirements of that track. In that case, the offeror shall include all proposed devices for that track within the single proposal submitted for that track. Offerors shall clearly identify the applicable award track in the proposal cover letter. Alternate proposals with differing pricing models or technologies from those required in this solicitation will not be accepted or evaluated. Basis for Award Proposals shall be submitted in accordance with the instructions outlined in Section L. Proposals that fail to comply with proposal submission requirements may be removed from further evaluation or consideration for award. The Government anticipates awarding a minimum of three (3) IDIQ contracts beneath each track (Fingerprint, Face, Iris, Palm, Multi-Modal) to those responsible Offerors whose proposals are most advantageous and represent the best value to the Government utilizing the Highest Technically Rated Offerors with a Fair and Reasonable Price (HTRO-FRP) award basis. There is no maximum number of IDIQ awards per track. These numbers are estimates, and DHS may increase or decrease the number of awards in its sole discretion. Using the HTRO-FRP award basis, the Government will evaluate the non-price factors to first determine the highest technically rated proposals beneath each track. The Government will then evaluate price for those Offerors determined to be among the highest technically rated proposals within each track to determine whether their proposed prices are fair and reasonable. The Government will select for award within each track the highest technically rated offerors with fair and reasonable pricing. If an offeror submits a proposal with multiple devices under a single track, each device will be separately evaluated and considered for award using a HTRO-FRP award basis. To be clear, the Government will not consider tradeoffs between price and non-price factors under the HTRO-FRP award basis. The Evaluation Factors are as follows: Factor 1 � Availability of Devices Factor 2 - Supporting Documentation (Not Rated) Factor 3 � Technical Approach Factor 4 � Price (Not Rated) Proposal Submission Proposals shall be submitted via e-mail to the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist on or before September 18, 2026 at 10:00 AM Eastern Time. Question Submission All questions associated with the subject solicitation shall be sent in writing to the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist no later than 10:00AM Eastern Time on September 14, 2026.

Point of Contact Jakisha Butts, Contracting Officer FCI Estill Federal Bureau of Prisons Email: j2butts@bop.gov All inquiries shall be submitted in writing via email. This notice is prepared in accordance with the format outlined in Subpart 12.1 of the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO). title: Commercial food delivery service for MSG
description: The purpose of this fixed price contract is to obtain food services program for U.S. Government at U.S. Embassy Tallinn for Marine Security Guards at the Marine Security Guard Residence (MSGR). Contractor will utilize its own facilities for the preparation, provide individually packed meals of food and deliver them to the residence. Contractor will be responsible for removing used food containers and any uneaten meals from the residence and disposing of them at contractor facilities during meal deliveries. The contract will be for a one-year period, from the date of notice to proceed. The Contractor shall furnish all managerial, administrative, and direct labor personnel that are necessary to accomplish the work in this contract. Contractor employees shall be on site only for contractual duties and not for other business purposes. 1.3 TYPES OF SERVICES Shall include the following work: 1.3.1 Contractor will be responsible for providing individually packed lunch and dinner meals for seven people per day (98 meals per week). 1.3.2 Contractor will use own discretion on when to transport meals to the residence in Tallinn. Request is to deliver three times a week. 1.3.3 Contractor will utilize its own operation hours for preparation, packaging, and delivery of food to ensure that (1) lunch and (1) dinner meal is available daily for seven people. 1.3.4 Contractor is encouraged to transport multiple day�s meals every trip to minimize daily transportation of meals. 1.3.5 Contractor will be responsible for removing used food containers and any uneaten meals from the MSGR and disposing of them at contractor facilities during meal deliveries.

title: Access Control Doors in support of 45th Medical Group (MDG), Patrick Space Force Base (SFB), Florida
description: The purpose of Amendment 0001 to Request for Quotation (RFQ) HT90626QE086 is to extend the quote due date from 4 September 2026 to 18 September 2026. This Request for Quotation (RFQ) HT940626QE086 is a sole source for the delivery, installation, and maintenance for an additional twenty-one (21) access control doors in support of the 45th Medical Group (MDG), Patrick, Space Force Base (SFB), FL. Notice of Intent The Defense Health Agency (DHA) intends to negotiate on a sole source basis in accordance with FAR part 12.102(a). For purchases not exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold, only one source reasonably available (e.g., urgency, exclusive licensing agreements, brand name, or industrial mobilization). The proposed source is Securitas Technology Corporation, 3800 Tabs Drive, Uniontown, OH 44685-9564. This acquisition is for the procurement of an additional twenty-one (21) access control doors, to include all-inclusive labor, personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform the installation and integration of the 21 access control doors with the existing Securitas server and Lenel software infrastructure and hardware utilized by the 45th Medical Group (MDG), Patrick, Space Force Base (SFB), FL. It is the contractor�s responsibility to be familiar with the applicable FAR and DFARS clauses and provisions. The FAR and DFARS clauses may be accessed in full text at the below-referenced addresses: FAR Clauses: https://www.acquisition.gov/browse/index/far FAR Overhaul: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul DFARS Clauses: https://www.acguisition.gov/dfars The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Codes: 561621 � Security Alarm Systems Sales Combined with Installation, Repair, or Monitoring Services This acquisition is for the procurement of an additional twenty-one (21) access control doors, to include all-inclusive labor, personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform the installation and integration of the 21 access control doors with the existing Securitas server and Lenel software infrastructure and hardware utilized by the 45th Medical Group (MDG), Patrick, Space Force Base (SFB), FL. The 21 access control doors must be integrated with the current existing Securitas server and Lenel software infrastructure and hardware for system programming and control. The contractor shall be responsible for the configuration of the new 21 access control doors with the existing Lenel software across multiple facilities/buildings within the 45th MDG. All access-controlled doors must be programmed to lock or unlock based on a time schedule provided through the Lenel software system integrated with the Securitas Technology server. Only Securitas Technology Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEM) certified and qualified technicians are authorized to perform the installation and integration of the 21 access control doors and service the Lenel software infrastructure and hardware. All installation, integration, software licensing, warranty, and services associated with the 21 access control doors, Lenel software, and all equipment shall be in accordance with OEM terms and conditions. The contractor shall provide installation and integration of the 21 access control doors and all services during normal business hours (i.e., 8 hours a day and 5 days a week), excluding United States Federal Government holidays, which are identified online at the following site: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/pay-leave/federa1-holidays/#url=2026. A request for documentation or additional information or submission that only ask questions will not be considered as an affirmative response. A determination by the Government not to compete based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement or to proceed with a sole source procurement. Responses Submission Capability statements are due by 10:00 A.M. ET, 2 September 2026. Capability statements shall be submitted by email ONLY as a Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF attachment to derrick.w.walker.civ@health.mil and jessica.l.horst5.civ@health.mil. title: MARSOC Advance Training Company (ATC)
description: Action: Notice of Intent to Sole Source Agency: U.S. Special Operations Command (USSOCOM) Contracting Office: Marine Corps Forces Special Operations Command (MARSOC) Classification Code: NAICS: 541611 � Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services PSC: R499 - SUPPORT- PROFESSIONAL: OTHER Subject: Intent to Award a Sole Source Contract for Marine Raider Training Center (MRTC) Advance Training Company (ATC) Full Time Equivalent (FTE). 1. Description of Requirement: The U.S. Marine Corps Forces Special Operations Command (MARSOC) intends to award a single-award Definitive Contract to Threat Tec LLC to provide precise and effective special reconnaissance operations that are fully coordinated and synchronized among all components of USSOCOM and key interagency organizations. The ATC program requires contracted support for exercise design, development, and management, scenario constructions, and tailored training support. The contractor shall provide formal training to individual Critical Skills Operators (CSO) in Advanced SR skills to provide qualified CSO�s to the Marine Special Operations Companies (MSOCs). The unit specifically charged with this responsibility is the MRTC. Due to the small size of the MRTC staff, contractor assistance is required to support the Special Reconnaissance, Instructor Sustainment Courses, and other Advanced SR Courses. The resultant contract will have a one-year basis for a total estimated price of $2,994,950.40. 2. Authority: This action is being conducted on a sole-source basis under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR Overhaul 6.103-1 for the acquisition of noncommercial services using Negotiated Contracting Procedures under RFO Part 15. 3. Rationale for Sole Source: Threat Tec, LLC is the incumbent contractor currently executing the MRTC ATC course curriculum, exercise design, full-mission profiles, and scenario development. An immediate bridge is required to prevent catastrophic lapses in specialized training pipelines for Marines Special Operations Companies (MSOCs) and Critical Skills Operators (CSOs) deploying to global operational areas. This bridge contract is essential to prevent a critical gap in mission-essential training services while USSOCOM finalizes, awards, and fully implements its comprehensive, enterprise-wide SOF Global Services Delivery (SOFGSD) contract in the fiscal year of 2027. SOFGSD will replace the prior SOF Core Support Services contract. The contract covers the full range of knowledge-based services supporting U.S.-based and globally assigned Special Operations Forces, from training and program management to intelligence support engineering and administrative services. Awarding an alternate contractor for this interim bridge period would introduce substantial, mission-degrading delays. The advanced ATC curriculum requires cleared, highly vetted personnel with existing institutional knowledge of MARFORSOC and USSOCOM Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures (TTPs). Any phase-in/ramp-up period would compromise active, scheduled course iterations. Transitioning to a new vendor for an interim period prior to onboarding onto the SOFGSD vehicle would result in significant duplicate mobilization and phase-in costs that cannot be recovered through competition. 4. Notice to Industry: All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation within fifteen (15) calendar days of publication of this notice, which shall be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Capability statements received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement in lieu of this sole-source action. 5. Submission Instructions: All capability statements must be submitted via email to the Contracting Officer, Jordan D. Orellana Buitron, at jordan.d.orellanabuitron.mil@socom.mil and Contracting Specialist, Ger Yang, at ger.yang.mil@socom.mil.

description: De VRT wenst per perceel één Opdrachtnemer te contracteren voor de levering van warmtebeeldcamera’s (WBC’s) en bijbehorende toebehoren. De WBC’s worden ingezet ter ondersteuning van brandbestrijding, technische hulpverlening en incidentbestrijding en dragen bij aan de veiligheid en effectiviteit van hulpverleners tijdens operationele inzet. De aanbesteding omvat de volgende percelen: • Perceel 1 – Decision Making Camera: warmtebeeldcamera voor gebruik onder zware en extreme omstandigheden, met nadruk op hittebestendigheid, robuustheid en besluitvorming tijdens inzet. • Perceel 2 – Situational Awareness Camera: persoonlijke warmtebeeldcamera voor oriëntatie in rook, detectie van thermische sporen en ondersteuning van de individuele veiligheid, met minimale bediening en een gewicht van maximaal 500 gram. Onder WBC’s en toebehoren worden verstaan: accessoires, laders, accu’s, software, onderhouds- en reparatiemogelijkheden, technische ondersteuning, updates en training. Raamovereenkomst; geen gegarandeerde afname.

description: PRESOLICITATION NOTICE ONLY - Proposed Solicitation Number - W9126G26BA010 posted on or about 18 September 2026. Contract for Joe Pool Dam Slide Repair at Joe Pool Lake, Texas. This announcement is a competitive small business set aside, firm-fixed price, Joe Pool Dam Slide Repair civil works construction services at Joe Pool Lake, Texas. The North American Industry Classification System code (NAICS) for this procurement is 237990-Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction which has a small business size standard of $45 Million. The Product Service Code is Z2PC-Repair or Alteration of Dams. The solicitation is anticipated to be issued on or about 14 September 2026, and proposals due on or about 15 October 2026. description: Engineering Services Firms for a Single Award Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Design Contract This announcement is for the selection of a single Engineering Services (ES) Firm for an Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Design contract for the Department of Veterans Affairs, Erie VA Medical Center located in Erie, Pennsylvania. Projects will be for the Erie VA Medical Center. Work will be required on an as needed basis and will be awarded by use of Firm Fixed Price Task Orders. The Government intends to award a Firm Fixed Price Contract. All potential offerors must provide a SF 330 containing all required information listed below. The form format must be the General Services Administration SF 330 found on the GSA Forms Library website. The resultant award shall be established as a single five (5) year contract. Total value of the contract shall not exceed $7,000,000.00 CONTRACT INFORMATION: The Engineering Services IDIQ contract may be used for a wide range of design services. Primarily the Task Orders will be used, but not limited to, design of new commercial/industrial type facilities and to design renovations of existing facilities. All contract awards will incorporate the attached Scope of Work dated June 16, 2026, attached. Expected ES services may require any combination of the following: Title I Site Investigation Services, Title I - Design Services, and Title II Construction Period Services. This contract is being procured in accordance with the Brooks AE Act as implemented in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 36.6, Veterans Administration Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) 836.6 and Veterans Affairs Acquisition Manual (VAAM) M836.6. Firms will be selected for presentations based on demonstrated competence and qualifications for required work. This contract is set-aside 100% for Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business s (SDVOSB) capable of completing work under the North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code 541330. A Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract will be awarded with a minimum $2,000.00 guarantee. The minimum guarantee for the entire contract term will be satisfied by the award of the initial Task Order. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: Interested firms having the capabilities to perform this work must submit an email copy of the Standard Form 330 (SF 330) Parts I and II. Please note this is not a request for proposal. Eligible responses received will be evaluated and the top three (3) most highly qualified firms will be compiled on a shortlist of candidates who will be contacted for an interview. For the evaluation, Professional Qualifications to Perform the Services Required, Specialized Experience and Technical Competence, are significantly more important than the other five (5) factors and are of equal weight. The remaining five (5) factors are of equal weight among themselves. The following evaluation criteria shall be used to evaluate firms and determine the most highly qualified firm for possible contract award. A. Professional Qualifications necessary for satisfactory performance: This is intended to evaluate the personnel and their related qualifications. The key positions should include Project Managers, Quality Assurance Manager, Architects, Structural Engineers, Electrical Engineers, Mechanical Engineers, Fire Protection Engineers, and Interior Designers. Firm should indicate whether these personnel have professional certifications in particular field, i.e. PE in Mechanical Engineering. The evaluation board shall consider the specific experience and qualifications (i.e., education, training, registration, certifications, overall relevant experience, and longevity with the firm) of personnel proposed for assignment to the project, and their record of working together as a team when evaluating professional qualifications. The lead designer in each discipline must be registered but does not have to be registered in the particular state where the project is located. B. Specialized Experience and Technical Competence: This factor evaluates the experience of the firm and design team in completing projects requiring skills similar to those anticipated for this contract. This may include general renovation of medical center space to include architectural changes of walls, ceilings, floors, finishes, carpentry, masonry, doorways including hardware, electrical, plumbing including storm sewer, sanitary, hot and cold water, Heating, ventilating, Air conditioning (HVAC) to include, package units, variable air and constant air volume terminals with reheat, Variable frequency drive air handlers, steam and condensate piping, primary and secondary electrical circuits, digital controls, fire protection to include sprinkle system, central fire and security alarms, audio paging systems, asbestos abatement and all work to return space to finished, functioning condition. Experience providing drawings in 3D. Designing general construction of new space to include structural work, roofing, exterior walls, site work, site utilities and work as stated above. Design of specialty construction may include tuck pointing, asphalt paving, elevators, complete key system, large centrifugal chillers and Boiler controls. Extra consideration may be given for experience designing projects for Department of Veterans Affairs Facilities. The evaluation board shall consider at least five (5) similar projects and how well the proposal addresses technical capabilities in design quality management procedures, CAD Building Information Modeling, equipment resources, and laboratory requirements for the firm and any proposed subcontractors. Where appropriate, the evaluation board will also evaluate their experience in energy conservation, pollution prevention, waste reduction and the use of recovered materials. The effectiveness of their proposed project team (including management structure, coordination of disciplines, subcontractors, and prior working relationships) should also be examined. NOTE: Ensure that projects listed were completed by the firm as the prime contractor and not as a subcontractor or projects completed by key personnel while employed by another firm C. Past Performance: Past performance on contracts with Government agencies (Particularly Department of Veterans Affairs) and private industry in terms of cost control, quality of work and compliance with performance schedules. When evaluating past performance, the evaluation board shall consider superior performance ratings on recently completed VA projects as well as the reputation and standing of the firm and its principal officials with respect to professional performance, general management, and cooperativeness. Also, consider, as appropriate, the record of significant claims against the firm because of improper or incomplete architectural and engineering services. D. Capacity to accomplish the work in the required time: This factor evaluates the ability of the Engineering Services firm to, given their current projected workload and the availability of their key personnel, to accomplish the project in the required time. When evaluating capacity, the evaluation board shall consider the volume of work awarded by VA during the previous 12 months. Use data extracted from the Federal Procurement Data System. Consider the full potential value of any current indefinite delivery contracts that a firm has as well. Also, assess the available capacity of key disciplines to perform the work in the required time. E. Location in the general geographic area of the project and knowledge of the locality: This factor evaluates the response time from the ES firms design office from the location of work to the Erie VA Medical Center. The personnel identified as the design team staff are expected to work in the design office identified for evaluation of this factor. NOTE: Time will be measured from the Erie VA Medical Center, Erie, PA via car to the firms indicated office where

description: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation - 70Z08526Q0027652 The United States Coast Guard Deputy Commandant for Systems (DCS) is issuing this combined synopsis/solicitation on behalf of the Surface Forces Logistics Center (SFLC) to award a firm-fixed-price service contract, as detailed in the attached Statement of Work. 1.1 Intent. The applicable Product Service Code is 2040 marine hardware and hull items. All services must be performed on-site at: CGC OAK 47 Chandler Street Newport, RI 02841 USA Period of Performance: 03/24/027 to 02/06/027 at homeport. The following factors will be used to evaluate offers: � Technical Capability (Pass/Fail) � Past Performance (Pass/Fail) � Total Price A quotation must receive an Acceptable rating for all non-price factors to be eligible for award. Among all acceptable quotations, award will be made to the responsible offeror submitting the lowest evaluated price. To establish Technical Capability (Pass/Fail), the quotation must demonstrate a clear understanding of the work statement requirements, conform strictly to all specifications in the attached Statement of Work, and provide any adequate capability and corporate experience documentation required by the solicitation. Failure to meet these criteria will render the quotation unacceptable. The Government will evaluate recent (completed within the last three years) and relevant past performance to assess the likelihood of successful performance. Past performance will be evaluated on an acceptable or unacceptable basis. To receive an acceptable rating, past performance must demonstrate a rating of satisfactory or higher performance of similar work. Offerors without recent or relevant past performance will be assessed as "Neutral" and considered acceptable for award. Past performance demonstrating marginal or below performance is unacceptable. Offerors shall identify all subcontractors anticipated to perform work under this contract. For each subcontractor, the offeror shall provide the subcontractor�s name, address, point of contact, phone number, the specific work items/specifications they will perform, and the percentage of work they will execute. Submit offers electronically via email to the points of contact identified in this notice. The Government does not prescribe a specific quotation format. Offerors must submit a quotation that clearly identifies the items offered and demonstrates compliance with the stated requirements. Submissions must be complete, clear, and presented in a format that allows effective evaluation by the Government. Submit all questions via email to the points of contact identified in this notice. The Government will not accept telephone inquiries. Submit offers on a firm-fixed-price basis. Prices must be all-inclusive and must cover all costs associated with providing the services, including but not limited to labor, materials, equipment, supervision, transportation, and any other costs. The Government may consider offers nonresponsive if they include conditional pricing, price escalation language, or statements indicating that prices are subject to adjustment based on future costs or fees. description: The integration of the dual-visor system in the T-6 aircraft will significantly enhance aircrew safety and operational efficiency by eliminating the hazardous requirement to physically swap visors during flight. By allowing pilots to seamlessly transition between clear and tinted visors, this upgrade mitigates the risk of introducing Foreign Object Debris (FOD) into the cockpit and drastically reduces "head-down" time and distraction during critical, high-workload phases of flight. Ultimately, this modernization ensures continuous eye protection against glare, bird strikes, or canopy fragmentation while maintaining optimal situational awareness, thereby directly lowering the mishap potential within the T-6 training environment.

description: Pre-Solicitation Notice for the notice of intent to award a sole source contract. This is not a solicitation. The Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Office of Research and Development (R&D), Regional Procurement Office (RPO) � East in Pittsburgh, PA intends to award on a sole source basis a Firm-Fixed-Price Contract for a one (1) year base period to include three (3) option years to Vertical Design, Inc., 1219 Derby Street, Berkeley, CA 94702, to develop and maintain a mobile application and specified server components in support of a research project for a four-year multi-site controlled clinical trial that studies the effectiveness of care coordination mobile (CCM). The vendor will work with the VA project team to develop and maintain a mobile application and specified server components in support of a research project for a four-year multi-site controlled clinical trial that studies the effectiveness of care coordination mobile (CCM), an intervention that uses passive mobile data monitoring, technological and motivational interviewing supports from peer specialists, and enhanced care coordination from VA clinicians to improve patient outcomes and reduce need for acute care services. These services need to be compliant and in accordance with several regulations including VACHS IRB regulations, Section 508 and ADA compliance standards, VA style guides, and grant-specified proprietary design characteristics. The awarded research project�s timeline requires services be provided by a company already fluent in the necessary regulations, standards, and style guides to minimize delays and ensure the protection of research participant data in the development and delivery of a usable clinical mobile application. Vertical Design, Inc. is the only known vendor that can provide the specialized services required. This is due to Vertical Design�s expertise, specialized knowledge, and proprietary rights in the development framework and underlying source code required to support the requirement, which is not available on the open market, and to Vertical Design being the named provider in the awarded research project�s approved IRB protocols. title: Lower Thames Crossing - Kent Roads - site Cleaning
description: The scope of works comprises the provision of all necessary management, supervision, labour, cleaning materials, consumables, plant and equipment required to undertake cleaning services at the Lower Thames Crossing (LTC) Kent Roads offices in Gravesend. The works will include maintaining the office accommodation, welfare facilities, kitchens, toilets, communal areas and associated spaces to a consistently high standard of cleanliness and hygiene, in accordance with the project requirements, agreed cleaning schedules and all relevant health and safety legislation. The subcontractor will be responsible for providing suitably trained and competent personnel, together with appropriate supervision, to ensure the services are delivered safely, efficiently and to the required standard. All cleaning products, materials and equipment must be suitable for their intended use and compliant with relevant COSHH requirements. All operatives undertaking the works must hold a valid CSCS card and Highways Passports. The Lower Thames Crossing is a new road that will improve connections between Essex and Kent through a tunnel beneath the River Thames. Our purpose is to drive change in how infrastructure is delivered-connecting people to jobs and businesses to opportunities, while leaving a lasting skills legacy for local communities and championing biodiversity and low-carbon construction. To support the project's ambitions, we are committed to publishing opportunities on Contracts Finder to provide full visibility to SMEs and local subcontractors. This widens access to the Lower Thames Crossing supply chain, encourages participation from smaller and locally based businesses, supports regional growth and ensures that organisations of all sizes have a fair opportunity to compete. Our ambition is to deliver the UK's greenest road while doing the right thing for local communities and the environment. Achieving this will require the support of our supply chain. Any supplier seeking to secure work on the Lower Thames Crossing must therefore demonstrate its commitment to supporting the following project ambitions: Leaving a skills legacy for the local community by recruiting locally and upskilling the workforce to enable meaningful progression into higher-paid and higher-skilled employment. Delivering the Lower Thames Crossing with the lowest practicable carbon, including supporting our zero-emissions ambitions, reducing the use of diesel on site and promoting alternative sustainable fuels and working practices. Creating opportunities through early-career roles, including apprenticeships, and inspiring young people to consider careers in construction through STEM engagement. Additional information: Please complete the attached expression of interest form and return to eleanor.clarke@skanska.co.uk

title: SOLE SOURCE: Snow Removal Services for the NWS WFO located in Caribou, Maine.
description: The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration�s (NOAA) Acquisition and Grants Office, Eastern Acquisition Division-Kansas City intends to negotiate and award a purchase order with Base plus four Option Years, on a sole source basis, under authority of RFO FAR 6.103-1, with the Town of Houlton for Snow Removal Services for the NWS WFO located in Caribou, Maine. Sole Source Justification: The Government intends to award a purchase order with base plus four option years to the Town of Houlton for the procurement of snow removal services due to their exclusive rights to the property in which the NWS WFO is located. The Town of Houlton owns and operates the Houlton International Airport where the FAA ASOS equipment is located. The Town Manager and the Public Works Director, have determined that all public works tasks at the airport shall be provided only by town public works employees. No other vendors or contractors are allowed on the airport site. Failure to have snow removal performed around and leading to the ASOS would prevent NWS technicians from performing required preventive and corrective maintenance during the snow season. A lack of observations would severely hinder, if not hinder completely, the government's ability to provide accurate terminal forecasts for safety of flight at the airport during adverse weather conditions. This pre-solicitation notice is not a request for competitive proposals and no solicitation package is available. However, firms that believe they can fully meet the government�s requirements may submit substantiating documentation or a request for additional information in writing to the (Contract Specialist) within 15 days after publication of this presolicitation notice. Such requests and documentation will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct this procurement on a competitive basis. A determination by the government not to conduct a competitive procurement, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the government. Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this pre-solicitation notice.

title: Draft SOW and PSpec for Extendable Boom Forklift (EBFL)
description: Amendment 01: The purpose of this amendment is to update the deadline for submitting industry questions and feedback regarding the Draft Statement of Work (SOW) and Performance Specification (PSpec) for the Extendable Boom Forklift (EBFL). The deadline for submitting the Q&A Matrix Template has been changed to September 03, 2026 at 12:00 PM EDT. __________________________ This posting announces the release of Draft Statement of Work (SOW) and Performance Specification (PSpec) for the Extendable Boom Forklift (EBFL), see attached. The primary objective of this notice is to provide industry partners with a comprehensive understanding of the mission requirements and submit technical clarification questions before the Government finalizes its formal Request for Proposals (RFP). It is important to clarify that the government is not currently soliciting or negotiating formal proposals through this draft. The focus of this phase is strictly on refining the acquisition's technical and administrative requirements to ensure clarity and feasibility. This draft SOW and PSpec remains non-binding, and all infoDraftrmation contained within is subject to further modification based on continued evaluation and industry input. The EBFL is a diesel-powered, rough-terrain telehandler engineered to transport, load, and unload tactical cargo weighing up to 11,000 pounds. A primary focus of this draft is the forklift's ability to operate reliably over uneven and severe terrain, including sand, snow, and mud, while handling sensitive payloads such as ammunition, general cargo, and expeditionary supplies. The draft specifications outline strict lifting and dimensional thresholds that the replacement vehicle must achieve. The system must support a rated capacity of 11,000 pounds at a 24-inch load center, or 7,000 pounds at a 48-inch load center, utilizing two separate quick-attach, detachable carriages capable of adjusting fork tine widths from 0 to 76 inches. Additionally, the draft mandates the capability to handle fully loaded 463L pallets (88x108 inches) weighing up to 10,000 pounds at a 54-inch load center. For standard logistics, the forklift must be capable of loading and unloading a 4,000-pound standard military pallet (40x48 inches) into an 8x8x20-foot ISO container elevated on a Marine Corps tactical vehicle or trailer, while maintaining physical compatibility with transport assets like CH-53E/K aircraft. All industry questions and feedback regarding these draft documents must be submitted utilizing the attached Q&A Matrix Templated (Attachment 1). Incomplete rows will not receive a Government response. Email Subject Line: EBFL Draft SOW/PSpec Questions -[Contractor Name]. All emails must adhere to the above format. Responses must be emailed to Stefanie Conway at stefanie.conway@usmc.mil no later than 03 Sept 2026@ 12pm EDT.

title: BONNET CARRE SPILLWAY ROTARY CUTTER SUPPLY CONTRACT St. Charles Parish, LA
description: The contractor shall provide Rotary Cutter mowing Units for Bonnet Carre Spillway as outlined in the Bidding Schedule and Material & Requirements Paragraphs. The contractor is responsible for purchasing and delivery of the units to the Bonnet Carre Spillway's project maintenance yard (16302 River Rd., Norco, LA). Furnish the number of tractor towed Rotary Cutters (Mowers) indicated in the bid schedule. Mowers shall have 15 foot total cutting width with two flexible wings. Cutting capacity shall be up to 5 inch in diameter with mowing deck minimum thickness of 1/4 inch. The transfer gearbox shall have minimum 250 HP and cutting gearboxes shall have minimum 225 HP. Input Drivelines and cutting Drivelines shall be Cat. 6. Wing decks must be able to flex up 90 Degrees and down 25 degrees. Mowers shall be capable of Tractor PTO Speeds of 540 or 1,000 RPMs. Cutting blades shall be minimum 1/2 inch x 5 inch. Deck shall include chains guards. Mower wheels/tires shall be solid tires and rims. Tires shall not be pneumatic, foam filled or laminated units. Submit quotes to Leann Thornton via email; Leann.R.Thornton@usace.army.mil

title: Draft SOW and PSpec for Extendable Boom Forklift (EBFL)
description: This posting announces the release of Draft Statement of Work (SOW) and Performance Specification (PSpec) for the Extendable Boom Forklift (EBFL), see attached. The primary objective of this notice is to provide industry partners with a comprehensive understanding of the mission requirements and submit technical clarification questions before the Government finalizes its formal Request for Proposals (RFP). It is important to clarify that the government is not currently soliciting or negotiating formal proposals through this draft. The focus of this phase is strictly on refining the acquisition's technical and administrative requirements to ensure clarity and feasibility. This draft SOW and PSpec remains non-binding, and all infoDraftrmation contained within is subject to further modification based on continued evaluation and industry input. The EBFL is a diesel-powered, rough-terrain telehandler engineered to transport, load, and unload tactical cargo weighing up to 11,000 pounds. A primary focus of this draft is the forklift's ability to operate reliably over uneven and severe terrain, including sand, snow, and mud, while handling sensitive payloads such as ammunition, general cargo, and expeditionary supplies. The draft specifications outline strict lifting and dimensional thresholds that the replacement vehicle must achieve. The system must support a rated capacity of 11,000 pounds at a 24-inch load center, or 7,000 pounds at a 48-inch load center, utilizing two separate quick-attach, detachable carriages capable of adjusting fork tine widths from 0 to 76 inches. Additionally, the draft mandates the capability to handle fully loaded 463L pallets (88x108 inches) weighing up to 10,000 pounds at a 54-inch load center. For standard logistics, the forklift must be capable of loading and unloading a 4,000-pound standard military pallet (40x48 inches) into an 8x8x20-foot ISO container elevated on a Marine Corps tactical vehicle or trailer, while maintaining physical compatibility with transport assets like CH-53E/K aircraft. All industry questions and feedback regarding these draft documents must be submitted utilizing the attached Q&A Matrix Templated (Attachment 1). Incomplete rows will not receive a Government response. Email Subject Line: EBFL Draft SOW/PSpec Questions -[Contractor Name]. All emails must adhere to the above format. Responses must be emailed to Stefanie Conway at stefanie.conway@usmc.mil no later than 27 August 2026@ 12pm EDT.

This is a Combined Synopsis/Solicitation Notice for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in RFO Part 12, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. The 90th Contracting Squadron is issuing this combined synopsis/solicitation, FA461326Q1054, as a Request for Quote using RFO Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 811310, with a small business size standard of $12.5M. The Government intends to award a Firm Fixed-Price, One-Time Service, Commercial contract. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAC) 2026-01 effective 03/13/2026 and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement Change 5/7/2026 effective 5/7/2026. DESCRIPTION OF ITEMS/SERVICES: This is a service contract to conduct a comprehensive compressed air system audit and analysis in Building 1235, Room 11 (East Side Mechanical Room) at F.E. title: NX EQ Hemodiafiltration Units
description: This Notice of Intent to Sole Source is not a request for competitive quotations or proposals. The Department of Veterans Affairs intends to negotiate and award a firm-fixed-price sole-source Requirements contract, in accordance with FAR 6.103-1(b), to a Large Business for the brand name Fresenius 5008XTM CAREsystem Hemodiafiltration Units and associated accessories. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 334510, Electromedical and Electrotherapeutic Apparatus Manufacturing, with a small business size standard of 1,250 employees. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 6515, Medical and Surgical Instruments, Equipment, and Supplies. The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 41 U.S.C. � 3304(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.103-1(b), �Authorized or required by statute.�. Interested parties may identify their interest and capability to meet this requirement. Any response must include sufficient detail to demonstrate the ability to provide all line items described below. No solicitation is available, and telephone requests will not be accepted. Responses received will be considered; however, the Government�s decision whether to compete this requirement based on responses to this notice remains solely within the Government�s discretion. The Government will not reimburse any costs incurred by contractors in responding to this notice, nor for the Government�s use of any information received. Requirement Description Hemodiafiltration Units are extracorporeal blood purification units used in renal replacement therapy and designed to combine diffusion and convection to remove uremic toxins, excess electrolytes, and fluid from blood. The unit operates by withdrawing blood from the patient through a vascular access line and circulating it through a dialyzer containing a semi-permeable membrane; small solutes diffuse across the membrane into a countercurrent flow of dialysate, while larger molecular weight substances are removed via convective transport driven by transmembrane pressure, with a controlled volume of plasma water filtered and replaced by sterile substitution fluid. Core components include a blood pump that regulates extracorporeal blood flow, a dialyzer (filter cartridge) that facilitates solute exchange and ultrafiltration, a dialysate delivery system that prepares and circulates electrolyte-balanced fluid, a substitution fluid system that infuses replacement fluid either pre- or post-filter, pressure monitors and sensors, air detectors and venous clamps, anticoagulation systems to prevent clotting within the circuit, and a central control unit with software that coordinates flow rates, pressures, fluid balance, and treatment parameters.

title: Electronic Key Box System
description: This service is for the procurement, installation, configuration, and commissioning of a modern electronic smart key box system to support secure, auditable management of physical brass keys used by the Security Services Office (SSO), the Security Operations Center (SOC), and other authorized CDC personnel. Many CDC facilities utilize brass keys either as the primary means of access (for non?PACS?controlled spaces) or as a redundant fallback method when PACS doors are unavailable due to power, controller, network, or hardware failure. Improving the 3 accountability and security of these keys is critical to protecting CDC assets, staff, and facilities. The purpose of this requirement is to strengthen the physical security posture of CDC facilities by deploying an enterprise class smart key management platform that: � Improves accountability and traceability of key issuance and return. � Reduces risk associated with loss, misuse, or unauthorized access to controlled keys. � Provides SOC with real?time visibility into key access events. � Supports PIV credentials and MFA methods, including PIN and/or biometrics. � Integrates seamlessly with CDC networks, SOC consoles, and SSO workflows. � Ensures operational continuity through backup power and controlled manual override capabilities. � Supports overall OSSAM/SSO mission readiness in alignment with CDC security policies. These systems will be installed and integrated at the following locations: � Roybal Campus, Building 20 (SOC) � 80-key capacity. � Roybal Campus, Building 17 � 40-key capacity. � Roybal Campus, Building 18 � 40-key capacity. � Roybal Campus, Building 23 � 40-key capacity. � Chamblee Campus, Building 106 � 40-key capacity. � Lawrenceville Campus � 20-key capacity.This project will modernize the outdated systems and processes CDC�s asset key control. The SOC manages access to all high value and restricted spaces mostly but also to regular calls for service of lockouts. The current key box is outdate and often fails through long down periods. Specialist are using manual and outdated procedures to issue key defeating the original intent of an electronic key control box. The number and placement of the boxes also reduces the risk of losing a key as well as traversing campuses across the metro Atlanta area.

The equipment must meet the technical specifications set in the technical evaluation criteria and include: • installation, setup, configuration, and commissioning of all equipment at the D85 Workshop; • Functional testing and verification of equipment performance following installation; • Provision of all required accessories, operating manuals, and warranty documentation; • Delivery of a minimum four (4) hour online training session for up to five (5) Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) personnel covering operation, maintenance, and software use; and • Warranty support, including parts and labour, for a minimum period of one (1) year. There are security requirements associated with this requirement. For additional information, consult 2.1 Security Requirement of the Resulting Contract Clauses, 3.6 Security Clearances, and 3.7 Security Documentation. For more information on personnel and organization security screening or security clauses, bidders should refer to the Security screening for government contracts - Canada.ca of Public Works and Government Services Canada (https://www.canada.ca/en/public-services-procurement/services/industrial-security/security-requirements-contracting/security-screening-government-contracts.html) website. The requirement is subject to a preference for Canadian goods and/or services. The Crown retains the rights to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada.

title: Assunpink Creek Site 8 Dam Rehab � NRCS-New Jersey
description: *Posting amended 9/3/2026 to add Attacahment 2 Drawings document to the Attahcments/Links. Posting updated project completion time to 180 days after notice to proceed is issued. Please see attached attachment/specifications document for further details. No Site Showing information at this time. Posting will be amended if site showing date/time becomes availlable. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotations are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 12FPC326Q0056 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for the Assunpink Creek Site 8 Dam Rehab for NRCS-NJ office. The objectives of this project are to rehabilitate the dam to meet or exceed state and federal dam safety criteria and to maintain the current level of flood protection provided by Assunpink Creek Watershed Dam Site # 8 by implementing the established design for rehabilitation. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 237990 The small business size standard is $40M. This acquisition is a Total Small Business Set-Aside. All responsible sources may submit a quotation which will beconsidered by the agency.
